coverage: Six editorial drafts from three repository-held extracted proceedings: May 27, 2008; June 25, 2012; August 10, 2026. Not an exhaustive corpus review. Original records and later developments require review.

sources.note: Extracted text read; original viewer and recording not verified in this build.
Filename and extraction header say June 28; proceedings body says June 25. Drafts use the body date and require date verification.
Historical action only; subsequent litigation and project status not established.

drops.title: Archive rewind: Cheyenne's 2008 out-of-state waste decision
drops.finding: The extracted May 27, 2008 proceedings record approval of a non-hazardous waste-disposal agreement with Waste Management Disposal Services of Colorado, Inc. The Public Works Director described approximately 47,000 tons annually and approximately $962,000 budgeted for first-year tipping and transportation costs.
drops.significance: This provides a historical starting point for examining disposal policy and costs over time.
drops.question: What later contracts and expenditure records show how the arrangement evolved?
drops.limits: Budgeted first-year costs are not audited expenditures. This record does not establish today's contract, costs, or disposal volumes.
drops.locator: Agreement with Waste Management Disposal Services of Colorado, Inc.; contract #5255
drops.excerpt: approximately 47,000 tons of waste per year

drops.title: Archive rewind: three more monitoring wells at Happy Jack Landfill
drops.finding: The extracted May 27, 2008 proceedings record approval of Modification No. 6 to Trihydro contract No. 4363, not to exceed $62,186, to plan and complete drilling of three additional monitoring wells at Happy Jack Landfill.
drops.significance: The action documents an earlier stage of the city's landfill-monitoring obligations.
drops.question: What do later monitoring reports and contract modifications document?
drops.limits: An approved ceiling is not proof of payment or completed work. Monitoring wells do not, by themselves, establish contamination.
drops.locator: Contract Modification No. 6 to Contract No. 4363, Trihydro Corp.
drops.excerpt: three additional monitoring wells at the Happy Jack

drops.title: Archive rewind: the 2012 DDA budget changed before adoption
drops.finding: Proceedings dated June 25, 2012 record a substitute Downtown Development Authority budget reducing the proposed total from $626,220 to $621,370. The substitute and amended main motion passed, recorded as Resolution No. 5403.
drops.significance: The record illustrates why the adopted version must be distinguished from the initial proposal.
drops.question: Which line items changed in the original and substitute budget attachments?
drops.limits: The extracted filename/header date conflicts with the proceedings body. Attachments and actual spending were not reviewed.
drops.locator: Resolution approving the DDA FY2012-2013 budget; #5403

drops.title: Archive rewind: sewer projects led Cheyenne's 2012 grant priorities
drops.finding: Proceedings dated June 25, 2012 record adoption of a substitute resolution correcting the order of Mineral Royalty Capital Construction Grant priorities. East Pershing sanitary sewer ranked first, followed by Crow Creek reclamation improvements, the maintenance facility addition, and Snyder Avenue sewer rehabilitation.
drops.significance: The order supplies a documented starting point for following historical infrastructure priorities.
drops.question: Which applications received awards and what projects were completed?
drops.limits: Priority ranking is not a grant award or completion record. The source date discrepancy remains flagged.
drops.locator: 2012 Mineral Royalty Capital Construction Grants; Resolution #5404
drops.excerpt: which was inadvertently listed in the wrong

drops.title: Archive rewind: two separate Roundtop-area ordinances
drops.finding: The extracted August 10, 2026 proceedings record final approval of annexation west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road as Ordinance 4691, and a separate BP Business Park zoning ordinance as 4692. Both entries record Moody voting no and the other members present voting yes.
drops.significance: Annexation and zoning were distinct actions; tracking their separate instruments helps avoid conflating decisions.
drops.question: What do the adopted ordinances and legal descriptions establish about the affected land?
drops.limits: These minutes do not establish parcel geometry, present ownership, a construction approval, or today's project status.
drops.locator: Third-reading annexation and BP zoning entries; #4691 and #4692
drops.excerpt: land west of Roundtop Road and south of Happy Jack Road

drops.title: Archive rewind: council authorized a referendum-law court question
drops.finding: The extracted August 10, 2026 proceedings record authorization for the City Attorney to investigate, prepare and, in professional judgment, commence a declaratory judgment action concerning whether annexation ordinances are subject to municipal referendum or an exclusive statutory challenge procedure. The motion carried with Moody voting no.
drops.significance: The action records authorization to seek a legal determination, not a judicial ruling.
drops.question: What subsequent court filings and orders resolve the question?
drops.limits: This drop does not establish that a case was filed, its outcome, or the current law. Later records require review.
drops.locator: Post-executive-session motion authorizing declaratory judgment action
drops.excerpt: whether an Annexation Ordinance is subject to the municipal referendum process
